verdict: Red 7/10 REJECT-as-tabled, blue 8/10 PARTIALLY OVERTURNED with the kill sustained on narrower grounds. Both benches land on FLAT, no starter, no pre-print position, so the recommendation is not contested - what blue overturned is red's reach, not its conclusion. The decisive finding is a test-design error: the thesis designated Q2'26 (printing ~8/26) as the first quarter fully exposed to China's April-2026 online financial marketing rules, and that is mis-dated. The eight-regulator Measures were issued 2026-04-24 but take effect 2026-09-30, at which point live-stream and short-video marketers must be employees of licensed institutions. Blue independently confirmed the dates. Management's 'no material impact' is therefore trivially true pre-effectiveness, and the marketing leg of the overhang cannot be adjudicated until Q4'26 prints around March 2027. Blue's correction is important and blocks a lazy read: red conflated two distinct overhangs, and only one is gated on 9/30. The other - the 报行合一 fee-wrapper reclassification - is already live on the carrier side, so the 8/26 print DOES test it. 'The print tests nothing' is overreach. The strongest surviving structural fact, sustained by both benches, is mix migration into the condemned wrapper: system-services fees are RMB904.6M, 68.8% of revenue, growing +39.8% against distribution's +27.8%, with carriers as the customer for both lines. The faster-growing 69% of the business sits in exactly the 'system maintenance cost' category regulators name as disguised commission - so the growth the thesis cited as evidence of health is the migration signature. Blue correctly tags the signature inference as interpretation rather than fact, and correctly keeps it at SIZING. Blue reduced the dividend and buyback finding: red's pro-rata arithmetic is confirmed (about $56M of the $58M went to the 96.8% insider base) but pro-rata payment does not unwind the point that cash demonstrably exited the PRC structure and reached ADS accounts, which refutes the transfer-restriction bear; and a buyback below 3.5x earnings is minority-accretive, so 'upside caps at a squeeze-out premium' is PLAUSIBLE only with no Cayman take-private step on the record. It stays a risk note, not a structure. What remains decisive for sizing is exitability, which no bench disputes: a ~$20M float against a US$15M buyback (roughly 75% of the float) at $196k/day of volume, in a 96.8%-controlled company. Blue's own new finding cuts pro-bull and should be carried: the licensing rule confines online marketing to licensed institutions and entrusted platforms, and YB is a licensed distributor, so the rule kills unlicensed competitor funnels - share consolidation upside exists, and 'the overhang can only hurt' is unproven. Whether YB's license class covers its short-video funnel is in the unread 20-F. Blue also flagged pull-forward contamination cutting pro-red: Q2/Q3 marketing spend may be pulled forward ahead of 9/30, so even a clean 8/26 print is upward-biased as a test. Blue reclassified the disposition under the response taxonomy as data-gap plus timing rather than a dead kill, and explicitly ruled RP_FAIR unavailable - fairness cannot be verified with carrier concentration and fee mechanics unread, and the wrapper tail is unbounded. That is the right frame: this is a park with two dated tests, not a permanent exclusion.
